trust_decision.summary: AuthController.redirect decides that a client-supplied redirect_uri stays on this host by stripping only '/' before prefixing HTTP_ROOT; CherryPy's HTTPRedirect then urljoins the result, and urlsplit drops tab/CR/LF, so '/\t/host' becomes the protocol-relative '//host'.

landing_point.why: The advisory names /auth/redirect, which maps directly to AuthController.redirect. It is the only handler of that name, and the whole flaw is in its last line.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP GET {HTTP_ROOT}auth/redirect?redirect_uri=... (also linked from login.html after signin)
same route; the fix adds @requireAuth() so unauthenticated users can no longer reach it (fix.diff:55)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists. Other HTTPRedirect calls build fixed HTTP_ROOT-relative targets, for example plexpy/webauth.py:192, plexpy/webauth.py:371 and plexpy/webserve.py:153, so there is nothing to dismiss.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A legitimate post-login return to a local path, including one that already carries the HTTP_ROOT prefix (stripped at plexpy/webauth.py:449-450), must still redirect. An over-broad fix such as an allow-list or a rejection of any '/' breaks the redirect=path round trip from check_auth through logout and login back to redirect.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: logout could redirect straight to redirect_uri when it is already logged out, instead of passing it on to the login form
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: logout already takes redirect_uri and issues an HTTPRedirect from it. A maintainer adding a 'skip login if auth disabled' shortcut could plausibly write that redirect directly.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: BaseRedirect could gain a generic 'return to' parameter, built the same way as auth/redirect
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: BaseRedirect already builds a redirect target from request args/kwargs, so a second path-joining redirect helper in another module would look natural.

O9_family: open redirect (CWE-601): parser differential (Python urlsplit strips tab/CR/LF, so a prefixed path turns into a protocol-relative URL)

O10_build.toolchain: Python 3 with vendored dependencies in lib/ (CherryPy, Mako, PyJWT)
O10_build.project_tests: None found: no test*/ directory with .py files in the pinned tree.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject a redirect_uri that starts with '//' or contains '://' before the strip, which misses the tab/CR/LF that urlsplit removes later.

out_of_scope_notes: plexpy/webserve.py:6839-6844 redirects to the raw REQUEST_URI with '/newsletter' replaced (when NEWSLETTER_AUTH==2). This is a different mechanism with no redirect_uri parameter, so it was not pursued.
unverified: Repo size in MB was not measured, because du could not be run with the available tools.

The defence was judged ineffective because the existing strip('/') was meant to prevent '//host' and was bypassed. This assumes CPython urlsplit strips tab/CR/LF (Python >= 3.9.5 / bpo-43882); the runtime Python version was not checked.
Backslash and other C0 controls were judged not exploitable after the HTTP_ROOT prefix, because urljoin keeps them in the path. That is a reasoned conclusion, not one checked by running code.
present_in_latest is not applicable, because no O8 routes exist and no latest release was provided.
